question: What is the primary focus of cancer epidemiology in healthcare?

options.A: Tracking disease frequency and distribution in populations
options.B: Discovering single-gene mutations in laboratory mice
options.C: Treating individual patients in hospital surgical wards
options.D: Manufacturing chemotherapy drugs for clinical trials

explanation: Epidemiology looks at populations rather than single patients to understand disease patterns. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why do health ministries rely on epidemiological data for public health?

options.A: To determine individual nursing shift rosters and pay
options.B: To calculate daily hospital food budgets for patients
options.C: To allocate medical resources and plan health infrastructure
options.D: To diagnose rare tropical infections in emergency rooms

explanation: Population data guides the distribution of healthcare resources where they are needed most. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which cancer types are among the most commonly diagnosed in Nigeria?
explanation: Breast, cervical, and prostate cancers form the bulk of the cancer burden in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is a primary reason for poor cancer survival outcomes in Nigeria?

options.A: Universal free healthcare covering all treatments
options.B: Late presentation of patients at health facilities
options.C: Excessive availability of advanced screening machines
options.D: Rapid genetic mutation rates unique to the region

explanation: Most patients arrive at advanced stages due to delays in seeking care and financial barriers. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h2)

question: What term describes the number of new cancer cases diagnosed in a population over a specific time?
explanation: Incidence specifically counts newly diagnosed cases during a defined period. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h3)

question: How does prevalence differ from incidence in epidemiological data?

options.A: Prevalence counts total existing cases, while incidence counts new cases
options.B: Prevalence only measures deaths, while incidence measures recoveries
options.C: Prevalence applies to animals, while incidence applies to humans
options.D: Prevalence is calculated weekly, while incidence is calculated yearly

explanation: Prevalence includes all current cases, whereas incidence tracks only newly diagnosed ones. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is an example of a modifiable cancer risk factor?
explanation: Smoking is a behavior that an individual can alter, making it a modifiable risk factor. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why is advancing age classified as a non-modifiable risk factor for cancer?

options.A: Age only affects infectious diseases rather than chronic ones
options.B: Medical science can easily reverse cellular aging processes
options.C: A person cannot alter the natural progression of getting older
options.D: Older adults never develop malignant tumors in clinical practice

explanation: Non-modifiable factors like age and genetics cannot be changed by personal choice or intervention. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h4)

question: What type of mutations account for the majority of cancer cases in human populations?

options.C: Somatic mutations acquired over a lifetime
options.D: Spontaneous mutations occurring only in red blood cells

explanation: Most cancers develop from acquired somatic mutations rather than inherited genetic traits. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h5)

question: How do environmental carcinogens typically initiate the development of malignant tumors?

options.A: By stimulating excessive calcium absorption in the bones
options.B: By increasing the total volume of red blood cells in circulation
options.C: By lowering the resting heart rate of the affected patient
options.D: By damaging cellular DNA and overwhelming repair mechanisms

explanation: Carcinogens alter DNA, which can lead to uncontrolled cell growth if repairs fail. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of cancer screening programs in public health?

options.A: Administering high-dose chemotherapy to patients with advanced tumors
options.B: Conducting post-mortem autopsies to determine exact causes of death
options.C: Providing palliative comfort care for terminally ill hospital patients
options.D: Detecting pre-cancerous lesions or early-stage disease in asymptomatic people

explanation: Screening targets healthy individuals to catch diseases early before symptoms develop. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) useful for cervical cancer screening in resource-limited settings?

options.A: It can cure the cancer without needing any surgical intervention
options.B: It requires expensive machines and specialized pathology laboratories
options.C: It is a practical and low-cost alternative to complex laboratory tests
options.D: It replaces the need for any healthcare personnel during the procedure

explanation: VIA provides an affordable screening option where advanced equipment is unavailable. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is a key responsibility of nurses in cancer epidemiology and prevention?

options.A: Educating communities and contributing to cancer registries
options.B: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs in industrial laboratories
options.C: Funding public health research grants for universities
options.D: Performing major surgical resections of malignant tumors

explanation: Nurses educate the public and help record accurate data for cancer registries. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why is accurate nursing documentation essential for cancer registries?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will never experience side effects
options.B: It automatically lowers the cost of hospital admissions for patients
options.C: It replaces the need for doctors to diagnose malignant diseases
options.D: It provides researchers with reliable data to track disease trends

explanation: Precise records allow epidemiologists to monitor cancer patterns and evaluate interventions. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h7)
